newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy mini-budget approved by Senate, becomes law.
newsitem.headline: Italy mini-budget approved by Senate, becomes law.

text.p: Italy's Senate (upper house) on Wednesday approved the government's 1997 mini-budget containing 15.5 trillion lire ($9.24 billion) of deficit-cutting measures, and it now becomes law, parliamentary officials said.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi has pushed through nearly 100 trillion lire of deficit cuts in the year since his centre-left government took office. The 1998 budget, due to be outlined on Friday, is expected to seek deficit cuts of 25 trillion lire.

Prodi has a clear majority in the Senate, where the vote was on a show of hands. The budget bill was approved in the lower Chamber of Deputies earlier this month after the centre-left government called a confidence vote.
Procedural rules in the Senate meant amendments to the package submitted by the opposition in the upper house lapsed on Wednesday, averting any need to make the vote a confidence test.

The government drew up the mini-budget to correct any 1997 overshoot in the target deficit, which Prodi says will be three percent of gross domestic product (GDP), the ceiling set for countries which want to join Europe's planned single currency.

Business groups and the opposition, as well as some of Prodi's own supporters, have criticised the mini-budget's emphasis on revenue-raising measures, including early payment by employers of taxes on severance payment funds which they hold.
